name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,309

entries.clue: Stars destroyed eg theatre bar (3,5,4)

indicators.note: a destroyed phrase has had its letters knocked apart and rebuilt

annotation.surface: A theatre bar has been wrecked, perhaps by celebrity stars on a rampage.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stars' pretends to mean famous actors in a theatre; it is a constellation. The 'eg' in the fodder looks like a throwaway abbreviation but supplies two letters.
annotation.definitionFit: The Great Bear, Ursa Major, is a constellation: a group of stars.

entries.clue: Play first reserve in chivalrous football team, we hear? (7,5)

indicators.note: what we hear is a sound, not a spelling

blocks.note: a football team has eleven players, so the first reserve is the twelfth man
a knight is the model of chivalry; said aloud KNIGHT is NIGHT
surface context that fixes the team at eleven players, so its first reserve is number twelve

annotation.surface: A question about who sits first on the bench for a gallant football side.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Football team' is there to fix the number: eleven players, so the first reserve is twelfth. 'Chivalrous' stands for the person, a knight, and only the sound is used.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Shakespeare's comedy of Viola, Orsino and Malvolio, named for the last evening of the Christmas season.

entries.clue: Lab seen changing permits (7)

indicators.note: letters that are changing move into a new order

annotation.surface: A laboratory is spotted in the middle of a refit, or a Labrador seen getting changed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Permits' reads as a noun, licences in a lab; it is the verb, allows.
annotation.definitionFit: To enable something is to permit it or make it possible.

entries.clue: Artist is beginning to enjoy Boost (5)

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: RA = Royal Academician, a crossword artist

annotation.surface: A painter starting to take pleasure in a lift in spirits.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Boost' is capitalised to look like a product or proper noun; it is the plain verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: lifting a price, a wage or someone's spirits upward all count as giving it a boost.

entries.clue: Fancier rose regularly spurned for trees (5)

indicators.note: every other letter is spurned, leaving the ones in between

blocks.note: the even-placed letters of these two words, 2nd, 4th, 6th and so on, survive

annotation.surface: A rose grower turns down trees in favour of flowers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fancier' looks like a comparative adjective but is the letter source; 'regularly spurned' throws out the odd letters, not the even ones.
annotation.definitionFit: Acer is the genus of maples, so acers are trees.

entries.clue: Flipping the bird at arrival time? (9)

indicators.note: flipping the letters tosses them into a new order

annotation.surface: Someone making a rude gesture at the moment a train or guest turns up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flipping the bird' is a rude hand gesture, which hides 'Flipping' as the indicator. The question mark flags 'arrival time' as a playful definition: the time you arrived in the world.
annotation.definitionFit: Your birthdate is when you arrived, in the sense of being born.

entries.clue: Plug from TV set remained broken (13)

indicators.note: broken letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: An electric plug pulled from a television that stayed out of order.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plug' and 'TV set' make an electrical picture; the plug is the promotional kind.
annotation.definitionFit: Plug is informal for a promotional mention, the kind a guest slips into an interview to publicise a book or show.

entries.clue: Look good ahead of Armstrong? (6)

indicators.note: one piece goes ahead of the other in the answer

blocks.note: Lance Armstrong the cyclist: the question mark admits it is a first name by example

annotation.surface: Admiring the view before an astronaut or cyclist comes into sight.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Armstrong' suggests Neil the astronaut first; it is Lance, the cyclist.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a quick peek or glimpse, the eyes resting on something only for a moment.

entries.clue: Get rid of backward content in Eminem review (7)

indicators.note: the word is written backward
the content of a word is what sits inside it

blocks.note: to axe is to get rid of
the rapper's name without its outer E and M

annotation.surface: Scrapping a hostile write-up of a record by the rapper Eminem.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Get rid of backward' reads as a phrasal verb; it is AXE turned round. 'Review' at the end is the definition, a verb, not the critic's piece.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the verb sense: inspecting or scrutinising something carefully, as a critic or auditor would.

entries.clue: Composer left after party (5)

indicators.note: the second piece comes after the first

annotation.surface: A composer slipping out once the party is over.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Left' reads as departed; it is just L, placed after RAVE.
annotation.definitionFit: Maurice Ravel was a French composer, best known for Boléro.

entries.clue: Artificial river in south-west and south-east (5)

blocks.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall, in south-west England

annotation.surface: Sounds like a report of a man-made river in the south-west and south-east.
annotation.walkthrough: The Fal runs through Cornwall, in England's south-west. 'In south-west' tells you which river, not where to put letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: teeth, eyelashes or a ceiling that are fake, made by people rather than grown or original.

entries.clue: Hot American has turned and fled (7)

indicators.note: turned letters run the other way

annotation.surface: An American on the run, perhaps a thief with stolen goods.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hot' in the surface means stolen or wanted; as the definition it means scorching, like the desert.
annotation.definitionFit: Saharan heat is the extreme heat of the Sahara, so Saharan can mean very hot.

entries.clue: Hard fabulist almost recalled prophet (5)

indicators.note: almost the whole word: its last letter goes
called back, so read in reverse

blocks.note: Aesop, teller of fables, without his last letter

annotation.surface: A tough teller of tales half-remembered as a prophet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fabulist' means a writer of fables here, not a liar, and the classic one is Aesop.
annotation.definitionFit: Hosea is one of the minor prophets of the Hebrew Bible.

entries.clue: Carriage left transport hub (7)

blocks.note: air = carriage, bearing, as in 'a regal air'

annotation.surface: A railway carriage has pulled out of a station.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Carriage' and 'transport hub' paint a railway scene; carriage is the way someone holds themselves, an air.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the place where planes, trains, buses and taxis converge, a centre of travel.

entries.clue: Some fancy an ideal poison (7)

indicators.note: some of the phrase, a run of letters inside it

annotation.surface: Some people are drawn to the perfect poison, as in a murder mystery.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Some' reads as some people, the subject of 'fancy'; it tells you to take some of the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a fast-acting toxic compound, famous from murder mysteries and its smell of bitter almonds.

entries.clue: Conservative posted approval (7)

annotation.surface: A Conservative politician has mailed in their sign-off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Posted approval' reads as publishing a thumbs-up; 'posted' is the past tense of mailing something.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: agreement or permission, given when someone says yes to a proposal.

entries.clue: A nun cries out for protection (9)

indicators.note: letters that are out are disordered

annotation.surface: A nun calls out for someone to protect her.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cries out for' reads as one phrase; split it after 'out', and 'for' is the link to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a policy that covers you financially against loss, damage or accident.

entries.clue: How much one gets from second career (5)

blocks.note: to career is to rush along, and a hare is something that careers

annotation.surface: Asking what a second job pays.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Career' reads as a job; here it is one who careers, charging headlong, and a hare fits.
annotation.definitionFit: Your share is how much you get when something is divided.

entries.clue: Vital organ not needing exterior organ (3)

indicators.note: the word's outside letters are not needed

blocks.note: the heart is a vital organ
hEARt with its outer letters H and T dropped

annotation.surface: A medical note that a vital organ can do without its outer covering.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Organ' appears twice: the first is the heart you start from, the second is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: hearing happens through this part of the body, one of the sense organs.

entries.clue: Sport where Tamworth might be out of practice (5)

blocks.note: a Tamworth is a breed of pig, kept in a sty

annotation.surface: A sports fan in Tamworth, an English town, whose team has not trained.
annotation.walkthrough: Tamworth is a town in Staffordshire, which the surface leans on, but it is also a breed of pig, and a pig lives in a sty.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: metal left unused corrodes, and skills left unused likewise decline.

entries.clue: She & he dare love madly, being so? (4,4,5)

definitions.text: She & he dare love madly, being so?

indicators.note: letters behaving madly are thrown about

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters; & is simply 'and' and adds nothing

annotation.surface: Two lovers take the plunge and are besotted with each other.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a couple who dare to love madly are head over heels. The ampersand is skipped in the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: The whole clue reads straight: a couple who dare to love madly are besotted, tumbling helplessly into romance.

entries.clue: Elf hasn’t observed Boromir at first (3)

indicators.note: only the first letter of each word is used

annotation.surface: A Tolkien elf failed to spot Boromir at first.
annotation.walkthrough: The Lord of the Rings setting points to a Tolkien elf; the answer is the old folklore word.
annotation.definitionFit: A hob is a hobgoblin, a mischievous elf or sprite.

entries.clue: Act like a bird and make tracks (4,2)

blocks.note: a bird in flight beats its wings: it beats it, the air
to make tracks is to leave; the answer is the slangy order to clear off

annotation.surface: Instructions to flap like a bird and then run off.
annotation.walkthrough: Both halves turn out to be about leaving: a bird beats its wings to fly off, and 'beat it!' tells someone to scram.
annotation.definitionFit: To make tracks is to leave, which is what 'beat it' means.

entries.clue: Thick end and middle of rye sandwich (5)

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central letter

blocks.note: the butt is the thick end, of a rifle or a snooker cue

annotation.surface: Assembling a rye-bread sandwich with the heel of the loaf.
annotation.walkthrough: A butty is British slang, especially northern English, for a sandwich.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional use: northern English slang for bread with a filling, as in a chip or bacon one.
